projects.name: NetKnight
projects.tagline: A local-first home network security system where AI can investigate and propose, but only a deterministic Rust policy engine can act.
projects.summary: NetKnight aims to give an ordinary household the protection of a small security operations team without sending its data to the cloud. It learns which devices, services and routines are normal for a home, investigates anything unusual, and explains each conclusion with the evidence behind it. The core design rule is that AI never touches the network directly: a Rust data plane forwards traffic deterministically and keeps working even if every AI component fails; Sentinel (detection) and Oracle (investigation) run unprivileged and can only propose; and a Rust policy engine alone authorizes typed, time-limited, verified and reversible actions. The development foundation is complete. Phase 1, a safe lab gateway, is in progress.
highlights: Safety by architecture: AI services run unprivileged and can only propose; every action is typed, leased, verified and reversible, and packet forwarding never depends on a model
One Protocol Buffers source generates Rust, Python and TypeScript clients, checked by a cross-language compatibility matrix against a frozen baseline
Fail-closed security gate in CI: secret scanning, OSV vulnerability audit and a dependency license inventory
Reproducible builds with exact toolchain pins, verified on Windows and Linux runners
Each design decision is recorded as an Architecture Decision Record, and every numbered task closes with written validation evidence

projects.name: Engawa
projects.tagline: A private AI assistant whose memory lives on your own hardware. Nothing leaves your home without your approval.
projects.summary: Engawa (en-GAH-wah) is named after the veranda of a Japanese home, the threshold between inside and outside, which matches its governing rule: local brain, selectively disclosed actions. It is a self-hosted personal AI built memory-first. An encrypted Knowledge Kernel keeps your documents, notes and the relationships between them on hardware you control, with fast, attributable search across all of it. Later phases add grounded local chat; several switchable assistants that share one private memory and can discuss a question together in a "Roundtable"; secure remote access; opt-in hosted reasoning that only ever sees content you approve; email, calendar and smart-home connections; voice; and bounded agents.
highlights: Encrypted Knowledge Kernel: a SQLCipher catalog and an XChaCha20-Poly1305 source vault are the single source of truth; search indexes and graphs are rebuildable projections
Hybrid retrieval over a Tantivy lexical index, Qdrant vector search and a Neo4j knowledge graph, with source attribution
Rust kernel sidecar behind protected local IPC, designed to have no outbound network access
Encrypted backup and recovery, lifecycle reconciliation and zero-downtime index rebuilds
Next.js Control Plane for knowledge search, provenance history, graph inspection and confirmed maintenance actions
Strictly sequential numbered tasks, each with an approved plan, validation record and focused commit
